mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive monthly observations
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.4 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.4pp in a single month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE jumps by >0.4pp in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and depresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both rise simultaneously for three consecutive months, it indicates a monetary tightening accompanied by inflationary pressure, which increases risk premia and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month MA for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 2% month-over-month, combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.3 percentage points, signals a demand shock with labor market weakening, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls >2% MoM AND UNRATE rises >0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in months where RSAFS drops >2% MoM and UNRATE rises >0.3pp simultaneously.
